rationale: #919: a macro-declared body comes in TWO grammar spellings, and both used to source every read at `global`. (1) `TEST(my_case, keeps_its_locals) {…}` parses as a `function_definition` whose declarator name is the macro and whose params are the macro's arguments (CP2 suppressed the symbol and pushed an ANONYMOUS scope, so `calls global -> real_fn` came out of the body). (2) `TEST_CASE("sectioned body") {…}` parses as an `expression_statement` with a MISSING `;` whose block is a SIBLING — no scope at all, so the body's locals (`case_local`, `section_local`) published as file-scope symbols and its reads were attributed to `global`. Measured on the two cpp corpora before the fix: 3,003 expression-statement bodies (5,680 leaked symbols, 27k global-sourced edges) and 716 function_definition bodies (93 such edges). The fix publishes the definition the heading WRITES as the scope name — the heading text itself, never an invented identifier (`TEST(format_test, enum)` generates `format_test_enum_Test::TestBody()`, which is written nowhere) — flagged `expandedFrom: macro-heading`, and excludes it from exports (every macro writing this shape generates an internally-linked function). The control `control_fn` is an ordinary `function_definition` and must be untouched; `real_fn`'s own read keeps its own scope.
